key_insight: A deep learning surrogate combined with stochastic generation and optimization enables fast design of polycrystalline microstructures that balance competing spall and yield strength targets.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a practical route to microstructure optimization when repeated crystal plasticity simulations are too expensive for design studies.
method: 3D U-Net maps 3D polycrystalline copper morphologies to full-field velocity histories from plate-impact CPFE simulations.
Derivative-free optimization searches the microstructure space using surrogate predictions instead of repeated high-fidelity solves.
A distribution-consistent reliability region based on MMD tracks when optimization moves outside the training-data manifold.
evidence_signal: Validated optimal designs matched CPFE with under 3% prediction error, and surrogate-driven optimization cut cumulative evaluation time by about four orders of magnitude.
watch_item: Performance depends on staying within a reliable distributional region, so out-of-distribution microstructures may need additional training data or stricter trust-region control.
paper_title: Deep learning driven framework for optimization of polycrystalline microstructures under competing strength requirements
